4. It is the case of plaintiff that suit land comprising 29 decimals of land of dag No. 3246 of District settlement khatian No. 458 and No. 63 Nancha Nagar Mouzajoma of dag No. 21 originally belonged to Amzad Khalasi. Amzad Khalasi sold 10.5 decimals of land out of 29 decimals of land to Abul Hasim. Joynal Abedin purchased 7.5 decimals, Sabina Khatoon also purchased 4 decimals and 7.5 decimals of land purchased by Bazaler Rahman from Amzad Khalasi. The suit land having been recorded in 63 No. Bancha Nagar Mouza in khatian No. 909 in the name of Abul Hasim 4 annas share in the name of Joynal Abedin 2 annas share, in the name of Sabina Khatoon 4 annas share, 4 ann as share in the name of Bazaler Rahman correctly. In getting settlement, in khatian No. 909, the name of Sabina Khatoon has been wrongly recorded. Sabina Khatoon out of her share, sold 4 decimals of land by saf kabala dated 27th Falgun, 1339 B.S. corresponding to 11-3-1933 to Arafatunnessa. Abul Hasim sold his 6 annas share comprising 10.5 decimals of land to Bazaler Rahman, Joynul Abedin in 4 annas share transferred 7.25 decimals of land to Bazaler Rahman. In this way, Bazaler Rahman with his 4 annas share, purchased 10 annas share, in total purchased 14 annas share of 25 decimals of land, died leaving 3 sons, defendant No. 1-3. Arafatunnessa having owner of 4 decimals of land died leaving 2 sons, Abdul Aziz Patwari and Abdul Hasim Patwari and daughter, Anwara Begum. Abdul Aziz Patwari purchased 6 decimals of land from Bazaler Rahman by kabala dated 17-4-1944. In this way Abdul Aziz Patwari having owner of 7.5 decimals of land by purchase and by inheritance, died, leaving son, Sherajul Islam, 3 daughters, Parul Begum, Minara Begum, Shamsur Nahar and wife, Fatema Bibi. Fatema Bibi, Sherajul Islam and Shamsur Nahar jointly by saf kabala deed No. 12950 dated 29-11-1990 transferred 3 and 5/8 decimals of land to plaintiff Sherajul Islam and Shamsun Nahar sold 3 and 5/8 decimals of land by registered deed No. 1295 dated 29-11-1990 to plaintiff. At the time of death of Hossain Ahmed, he was survived by son, Shahab Uddin and daughter, Sabina Khatoon. On the death of Anwara Khatoon, her two sons, Shah Alam and Bachu Mea became owner of her property. Shahab Uddin, Shah Alam and Bachu Mea sold 3 decimals of land by baina, which was converted to registered document dated 20-4-1991. In this way plaintiff become owner by purchase and by inheritance of the scheduled land. After purchase, plaintiff went to pay rent to the local Tahsil Office on 15-2-1991 and came to know that out of suit land, during MRR survey, 29 decimals of land recorded in the name of his predecessor of No. 63 Bancha Nagar Mouza, Khatian No. 767, dag No. 8351. For total land of 29 decimals, plaintiff came to know that for aforesaid land in Mutation Case No. 111983-84 of the court of Assistant Commissioner (Revenue) the name of Bazaler Rahman was replaced and was recorded in the name of defendant Nos. 4-5 in holding No. 2405, khatian No.2404 and holding No. 2395 and khatian No. 2396. It is further case of plaintiffs that for the aforesaid wrong recording either in the name of Bazaler Rahman or in the name of defendant Nos. 3-4 or defendant No. 1-5, title, interest and possession of plaintiff has not been effected as the plaintiff purchased the suit land finding title of his predecessor and plaintiff could not know of the aforesaid wrong recording. The aforesaid wrong recording a cloud has been cast upon title of plaintiff which required to be removed, as such, plaintiff instituted the suit. For the cause of action of suit plaintiff has stated as :- 

 7.	The case of defendant Nos. 8,9 and 10 is that suit land consisting of 29 decimals recorded in PS khatian No. 909 and District Survey khatian No. 449 was demarcated as Abul Hasim in 6 anna, Joybul Abedin in 6 anna, Bazaler Rahman in 4 anna and Sabina Khatoon in 2 anna, with joma of Taka 2.25 which has been wrongly recorded in PS survey. JoynalAbedin in 4 annas share got 7.25 decimals of land and as plaintiff transferred his share to Bazaler Rahman and became titleless. Sabina Khatoon by registered kabala dated 27th Falgun, 1339 BS corresponding to 11-3-1933 transferred his share to Joynal Abedin and become titleless. Anjunnessa as mother of Bazaler Rahman, lived in joint mess and having satisfied with the nurse of Bazaler Rahman, transferred her entire purchased land i.e. 3 and 5/8 decimals of land to Bazaler Rahman at first week of January, 1935 orally and become titleless. As aforesaid, Bazaler Rahman become owner of 10 annas share, consisting of 18 and 1/8 decimals of land. Thereafter for ejmali land, Bazaler Rahman and Abul Hasim amicably partitioned and registered deed was executed on 24th Badra 1344 BS and registered on 10- 5-1937. In that partition deed Bazaler Rahman was settled with 10 annas and Abul Hasim was settled by 6 annas of land. While defendant in possession, Abul Hasim on 27th Badra, 1348 BS corresponding to 13-9-1941 executed and registered saf kabala deed transferring 2 decimals of land to Bazaler Rahman. While Abul Hasim was in possession on remaining 8 and 7/8 decimals of land, by saf kabala deed dated 23-1-1942, transferred the suit land to Jabed Ullah and become titleless. In that deed it was mentioned 10.5 decimals of land but in fact, Jabed Ullah got possession for 81/8 decimals of land. Jabed Ullah on 28-4-1944 by saf kabala deed, transferred the said land to Bazaler Rahman and became titleless. In this way, Bazaler Rahman became owner of entire 29 decimals of land. MRR khatain was prepared for the aforesaid land in the name of Bazaler Rahman and recorded in MRR khatian No. 767 correctly and was published accordingly. The entire claim regarding suit land of plaintiff against this fact is totally false and without any basis. Bazaler Rahman to the very knowledge of his brother, sister and of entire locality, possesses the said land i.e. 29 decimals for more than 12 years and his title became perfect. Bazaler Rahman died leaving 4 sons, defendant Nos. 1-3 and Sukku Mea who inherited his land. The case of plaintiff that Bazaler Rahman died leaving 3 sons is totally false each sons of Bazaler Rahman got 7.25 decimals of land. Subsequently, Nasir Ahmed, defendant No.3, sold 1 decimal ofland to Majibullah by safkabala dated 1-2-1960. Again, this Majibullah by kabala dated 23-10-1961 transferred 1 decimal of land to Ali Ahmed. Momin Ullah through his father, as heir, got 7.25 decimals of land, having title and possession, by saf kabala dated 22-6-1959 transferred 1 decimals of land to Ahmed Ali. Momin Ullah and Nasir Ahmed, defendant No.2 and 3 on 21-5-1960 by safkabala deed transferred 13 decimals of land to Ali Ahmed and delivered possession and also become titleless. Taher Ahmed and Chukku Mea, another two sons, through their father, Bazaler Rahman, inherited 14.5 decimals of land, which they sold to Lutfunnessa by registered saf kabala dated 27-8-1960 and became title less. Ahmed Ali being owner and possessor of his purchased land, by deed of gift dated 24-7-1967 transferred the said land to Lutfunnessa and became titleless. Although in that deed of gift, it is written 26 decimals of land but in fact Lutfunnessa got more land legally as got by donor, Ahmed Ali. In this way, Lutfunnessa become owner of 29 decimals of land. Lutfunnessa on 16-11-1972 by two saf kabala deeds, transferred entire 29 decimals of land to HasinaAkter and AKM Mohammad Ullah, defendant No.5, who mutated their names in Mutation Case No. 1/1983-84 and 2/1983-84 and separated joma and opened khatian No. 2395 and 2396. It may be mentioned, against the purchase of Hasina Akhter, AKM Mohammadullah, Oaziullah and Monir and other as co-sharer of adjacent land, filed Miscellaneous Case No. 206 of 1980 and 245 of 1974 for pre-emption and both the cases were dismissed on 1-7-1980. Hasina Akhter and AKM Mohammadullah possessed the said land for more than 12 years with the knowledge of all and perfected their title. AKM Mohammadullah, while in possession, having title of 14.5 decimals of land by kabala dated 9-6-1990 transferred the said land to defendant Nos. 8,9 and 10 by exchange and delivered possession. Ahmed Ali also exchanged 14.5 decimals of land on 9-6-1990 with defendant No. 10 and become titleless. Defendant Nos. 8,9 and 10 after getting the land as aforesaid, by Mutation Case No. 97/90-91, mutated their names, opened khatian and payed rents regularly till now. In the suit land plaintiffs have no right, title and interest. 

 13. Learned Assistant Judge while dismissing the suit holding inter alia that gift in favour of Bazaler Rahman by his mother Arafatunnessa in 1935 with deliver of possession has been proved by exhibits 2 (Chha) and admitted by defendant Nos. 8-10 and plaintiff; plaintiff also proved that Bazaler Rahman is the owner of 26.5 decimals of land which is also admitted; on consideration of exhibit (Ga) learned Judge found that there was mutual settlement about the land between Bazaler Rahman and Abul Hasim by partition deed dated 10-5-1937, where it was amicably settled that Bazaler Rahman will got 10 annas, Abul Hasim will get 6 annas which is also an admitted position; by registered kabala dated 28-4-1944 exhibit (Ga) to (Ga) 15, Bazaler Rahman purchased 6 annas share from Abul Hasim. Learned Judge also considered the deposition of PW 2, Ali Ahmed and held that it is admitted position that Bazaler Rahman become 16 annas title holder of suit khatian. Learned Judge also considered that at the time of MRR survey the other daughters and sons of Arafatunnessa were alive but they did not raise any objection against 16 annas ownership of the suit land in favour of Bazaler Rahman. Defendant Nos. 8,9 and 10, it is found by the learned Judge that by document, proved oral gift in favour of Bazaler Rahman which has been supported by exhibits 2(Cha) to 2(Jha) to Neo that plaintiffs purchased suit land from the successive heirs of Arafatunnessa. Thereafter, learned Judge discussed oral evidence of the witnesses and found that DWs 2, 3 and 4 proved Bazaler Rahman had 4 other brothers and one sister and also learned Judge considered the deposition of PWs 1 and 2 who admitted that the name of husband of Arafatunnessa and father of Bazaler Rahman was Ayub Ali, which is the case of defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10. Defendant No.9 as sharer, title holder, by exhibit 2 Chha, sold 6 decimals of land, which plaintiffs purchased from Anwara Khatun. Defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 claimed this deed as false, fabricated and not-binding upon, and in their depositions and written statements demand from plaintiffs to produce original deed but plaintiff did not produced and plaintiff did not give any explanation either orally or in the plaint as to why they did not produce this deed in evidence. Plaintiff also did not produce the deeds dated 7-6-1944 and 9-6-1944 in its original and it is also found by the learned Judge that by the deed dated 7-6-1944, and 9-6-1944, the predecessor of plaintiff exhausted his title of the exchange land and thereby from purchase from Anwara Khatun plaintiff did not acquire any title. Learned Judge also considered the depositions of the witnesses and found that neither PW 1 nor PWs 2 and 3 in their earlier depositions did properly describe the scheduled land and also found that PW 3 is the neighbor of the suit property. Learned Judge found witnesses of defendant Nos. 8-10 reliable. Learned Judge also found plaintiffs did not prove the PS khatian which was prepared wrongly and not created which has presumptive value. Learned Judge also found that plaintiff did not prove title of i.e. 4 sons and daughter of Amjad Khalasi and by deed plaintiff admitted PS Jorip. Learned Judge also found that plaintiff did not prove MRR khatian as wrongly recorded. Learned Judge also considered that plaintiff raised objection against Mutation Case and separated joma as a whole on 27-7-1983 but failed to prove that said recording was wrong and illegal and PW 1 did not state anything about their said mutation and separation of joma. Learned Judge also found that plaintiff although demanded but did not pay advelorem court fees as such the suit is not maintainable as per Order VII, rule 11 (c) read with section 149C of the Code of Civil Procedure. Learned Judge on consideration of depositions of witnesses ultimately held as:- 

 14. Plaintiff and Abdul Barek alias Manik Mea filed Title Appeal Nos. SO of 1997 and 21 of 1997. Both these appeals were heard analogously by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Laxmipur who by judgment and decree allowed both the appeals and decreed the suit. Learned Judge in the body of the judgment found that it is admitted fact that 29 decimals of land of District Survey Khatian No. 458, plot No. 3246 originally belonged to Amzad Khalasi. Learned Judge on consideration of exhibit 2-2(Ka) decided the share of Sabina Khatoon at 4 decimals of land. Learned Judge thereafter considered the case of defendant Nos. 8-10 that they claimed that Arfatunnessa orally gifted her 4 decimals of land to Bazaler Rahman but that oral gift was not at all proved. Learned Judge in support of such findings held that, principle of law that to prove gift, 3 essential ingredients must be proved, i.e. (i) there must have a declaration, (ii). acceptance of said declaration or offer and (iii) delivery of possession. It is settled principle of law that without delivery of possession no gift has been proved. Learned Judge found gift was executed in 1935 and Bazaler Rahman sold it by exhibit 2 Cha in 1944 but Bazaler Rahman did not make any respectful ground in exhibit 2 Cha that he got suit land by oral gift. Learned Judge also considered that bantaknama dated 10-5-1937 also did not mention in the recital of oral gift. Learned Judge considered that learned Judge of trial court committed gross illegality in not considering certified copy, exhibit 2 Cha dated 17-4-1944, in absence of original or in absence any explanation is in admissible, reversing that such finding of trial court as perverse as plaintiff stated that the said deed is aged about 50 years and the validity of said deed has not been challenged by Bazaler Rahman or his heirs as such at present, the validity of the deed cannot be questioned. Learned Assistant Judge took exhibit 2 Chha as illegal and on consideration exhibit 2 Cha dated 17-4-1944 learned Judge of the appellate court found that Abdul Aziz got 6 decimals of land and plaintiff purchased said 6 decimals of land from the heirs of Abdul Aziz, which plaintiff clearly proved and also proved possession of the plaintiff. Learned Judge also considered that defendant Nos. 8-10 claimed that Arafatunnessa had two other sons which had not been proved. Learned Judge thereafter found all the witnesses of plaintiff reside in and around of the suit land and witnesses of defendants are not adjacent to the suit land and people of suit property. Learned Judge also considered that Anwara Khatoon, daughter of Arafatunnessa, got 1 decimals of land through pre-emption case No. 147 of 1963 which was allowed on 8-6-1963, exhibit Chao. On these findings learned Judge found title of plaintiff and decreed the suit.
